title: Reckoning Note of the Premium Accounting Office: Premium Relief Credited on a Ridgecrest Advantage Premium Account
content:
The premium relief credited to a member is what the plan gives back on the plan premium account of a Ridgecrest Advantage Medicare Advantage Health Plan enrollment where more plan premium has been charged on it than the member is liable for, because the low income premium subsidy the member has been awarded reduces the plan premium of a plan that carries prescription drug coverage while the full premium is still charged.

### The quantities

1. **The premium relief credited to a member** is the plan premium reckoned on the account, less the plan premium the member is liable for, less the relief already set off, rounded to the nearest cent once at the end, and it is never less than nothing.
2. **The plan premium reckoned on the account** is the most recent plan premium charge standing on it.
3. **The plan premium the member is liable for** is the coverage months chargeable to the member multiplied by the plan premium of one coverage month.
4. **The coverage months chargeable to the member** are the coverage months reckoned as owed less the coverage months the low income premium subsidy award reaches back over, and are never fewer than none.
5. **The coverage months reckoned as owed** are the whole months that have passed since the coverage effective date, and one more for the month in hand.
6. **The plan premium of one coverage month** is the monthly plan premium of the plan held taken at the share of it the member meets, rounded to the nearest cent.
7. **The share of the monthly plan premium the member meets** is the whole of it, that is 100 per cent of it.
8. **The low income premium subsidy award** reaches back over no coverage months, that is over 0 coverage months.
9. **The relief already set off** is nothing.

The rounding to the nearest cent happens once, on the figure reached at the end, and not on the parts as they are taken.

### How the credit reaches the account

The credit names the single plan premium charge it relieves and the reason it was granted, and the full plan premium stays charged on the account so that what the member owes is always the charge less the credits posted against it. The relief owed is posted as a single credit entry naming the most recent plan premium charge standing on the premium account, whatever the size of that charge, so that the relief reaches the account in one entry rather than being split across the charges it relieves. The reason recorded with the credit is the low income premium subsidy the member has been awarded.

### Worked through on hypothetical figures

Take an enrollment whose coverage effective date is 1 January, a handling date of 20 March, a monthly plan premium for the plan held of 60.00 USD, and a most recent plan premium charge standing on the premium account of 260.00 USD.

- Coverage months reckoned as owed: two whole months have passed since 1 January, and one more for the month in hand, so 3.
- Coverage months chargeable to the member: 3 less the 0 coverage months the award reaches back over, so 3.
- Plan premium of one coverage month: 60.00 USD taken at the whole of it, so 60.00 USD.
- Plan premium the member is liable for: 3 multiplied by 60.00 USD, so 180.00 USD.
- Premium relief credited: 260.00 USD less 180.00 USD less nothing set off, rounded to the nearest cent at the end, so **80.00 USD**.
